cve_summary: The TS_OBJ_print_bio function in crypto/ts/ts_lib.c in the X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP) implementation in OpenSSL through 1.0.2h allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and application crash) via a crafted time-stamp file that is mishandled by the *openssl ts* command.
commit_message:
Fix OOB read in TS_OBJ_print_bio().

TS_OBJ_print_bio() misuses OBJ_txt2obj: it should print the result
as a null terminated buffer. The length value returned is the total
length the complete text reprsentation would need not the amount of
data written.

CVE-2016-2180

Thanks to Shi Lei for reporting this bug.

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
docstring:
/**
 * Summary: Prints the textual representation of an ASN1_OBJECT to a BIO stream.
 * 
 * Parameters:
 * bio (BIO*): The BIO stream to which the object representation will be printed.
 * obj (const ASN1_OBJECT*): The ASN1_OBJECT to be converted to a string.
 * 
 * Returns: int - Returns 1 on success, indicating the object was printed.
 * 
 * Logic: The function converts the ASN1_OBJECT to a string using OBJ_obj2txt and 
 * then prints the resulting string to the specified BIO stream using BIO_printf.
 */
